pharm: Fluoroquinolone; inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV
quick: Reduce to 160 mg daily if CrCl <=40
summary: Gemifloxacin (Factive) is an oral broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibacterial used for acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and mild-to-moderate community-acquired pneumonia in adults. The usual dose is 320 mg once daily. Like all fluoroquinolones it carries class boxed warnings for disabling and potentially irreversible tendinitis/tendon rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, and worsening of myasthenia gravis, so it should be reserved when alternatives are unsuitable.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis (adults)

dosage.c: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis

dosage.t: 5 days (7 days for certain pathogens, e.g., MDR S. pneumoniae, K. pneumoniae, M. catarrhalis)

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Separate from antacids, sucralfate, iron, zinc and multivitamins with metals by at least 3 hours before or 2 hours after
Reserve for infections without suitable alternative therapy
moa: Inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication, transcription, repair and recombination; bactericidal.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to gemifloxacin or any fluoroquinolone
relative: History of myasthenia gravis (may worsen muscle weakness)
Known QT prolongation or use of QT-prolonging drugs
History of tendon disorders related to quinolones

preg: Avoid unless benefit outweighs risk; quinolones affect cartilage in juvenile animals.
lact: Avoid; fluoroquinolones are expected to distribute into human milk.
renal: Reduce dose to 160 mg once daily when CrCl <=40 mL/min and in patients on hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment needed for mild to moderate hepatic impairment; data limited in severe impairment.

major: QT-prolonging drugs (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics) — additive QT prolongation, torsades risk
Corticosteroids — increased tendon rupture risk, especially in elderly
moderate: Multivalent cations (antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, calcium) — markedly reduce absorption; separate dosing
Warfarin — possible enhanced anticoagulation; monitor INR
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid co-administration with cation-containing products.
interactions.diagnostics: May affect some opiate/urine assays (class effect).

common: Rash (more common with longer courses, in women <40 and on HRT)

monitoring: Tendon, joint or muscle pain (stop drug if suspected tendinitis)
counsel: Take once daily and finish the full course
Separate antacids, iron, zinc and dairy supplements by several hours
Stop and call your doctor for tendon pain, swelling or snapping
Report numbness, tingling, weakness, confusion or seizures
Avoid strong sun and use sunscreen
Report a rash promptly, especially in the first week
pearls: Not currently in the openFDA database; data per Factive U.S. prescribing information / SmPC
Class fluoroquinolone boxed warnings: tendinitis/rupture, peripheral neuropathy, CNS effects, myasthenia gravis exacerbation
Reserve for patients with no alternative treatment options
Rash is more frequent than with other quinolones, especially with courses beyond 7 days in younger women
Separate from multivalent cations to preserve absorption
missed: Take as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one. Do not double the dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Provide supportive care, ensure hydration, and observe with ECG (QT) monitoring; hemodialysis removes only a modest fraction.
